hub_wide.brief: The fortnight is dominated by two intersecting regulatory flashpoints that create immediate advisory pull. Julie Bishop's public resignation from the ANU Council — alleging 'coercive threats' and 'overreach' by TEQSA, compounded by The Saturday Paper's exclusive that legal advice on regulator conduct was withheld from the council — has ignited the most politically exposed governance dispute in Australian higher education in a decade; every university board chair is now re-examining their regulator relationship and independence frameworks, and KPMG must be in those conversations within days. Simultaneously, TEQSA is broadening its technical reach through gen AI compliance guidance and education agent commission oversight, meaning the compliance surface for providers is expanding even as the regulator's conduct is under parliamentary and media scrutiny — a dynamic that prolongs advisory demand. The Australian Tertiary Education Commission's 'More Joined-Up Tertiary System' Discussion Paper and the Tertiary Roadmap consultation signal a structural redesign of the sector architecture that will require implementation advisory at scale once policy direction firms. DEWR's Employment Services Reform is the sleeper BD story this fortnight: the volume of reform collateral — new triaging methodology, Employment Goal Plans, Lived Experience Panel, and a National Press Club address — signals a reform programme entering its design-to-delivery inflection, where KPMG's workforce, service design, and implementation advisory capability are directly competitive. HVNL fatigue reform guidance landing in Big Rigs confirms the heavy vehicle sector is entering a compliance mobilisation phase, consistent with the transport brief's safety culture and L&D advisory opportunity. BD effort this fortnight should concentrate on education governance and DEWR reform advisory as the two highest-conviction, time-sensitive openings.
